title: Runtime Registry and WLU Integration
summary: Runtime Registry uses an optional WLU bridge to perform admission accounting before invoking dynamic capabilities.
why: Ensures that the cost of a capability is reserved and verified *before* the capability is executed, allowing for a clean HTTP 429 response.
invariants: Execution order: Resolve Session -> Validate Schema -> WLU Admission -> Invoke Capability -> Settle WLU.
A WLU refusal is returned as HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
Dynamic capabilities only receive a restricted metering surface; they never get the WLU authority itself.
